## Raw data are hard to interpret {#sec-rawdata}

Imagine coming home from an experiment. 
Data-table in Excel.
Hard to oversee; how to make sense of this?

At least three common techniques:

1. Summarize the distribution of your observations 
  using frequency tables.
2. Visualize the data with graphs or charts.
3. Calculate insightful summary statistics, 
  such as the mean of your measurements.

Below, we discuss each of these in turn.
However, because each of these methods depend
  on the type of variable that we're interested in,
  we first discuss the various types of variables
  that we must distinguish.
